text: {"status":"supported","evidence_ids":["ev-0170b0f63d871c8acab55668"],"request_dft":false,"proposed_test_ids":[],"rationale":"The claim is limited to the two recorded static sigma-zero energies, and ev-0170b0f63d871c8acab55668 records both. I rechecked the arithmetic. Alpha: -670.89296251 eV / 108 atoms = -6.2119718751 eV/atom. Pbcn: -1341.77791177 eV / 216 atoms = -6.2119347767 eV/atom. Alpha is lower by 3.71e-5 eV/atom, which is about 0.037 meV/atom, so the stated claim holds. This is a property claim about two recorded calculations, not a thermodynamic_stability or energy_ranking claim, so the hull and MLIP requirements do not apply. The scope statement itself says the result is not a convergence-qualified polymorph ranking. The two calculations use different k-meshes (Gamma 3x4x3 and Gamma 4x2x2) and the numerical_convergence field is empty. A 0.037 meV/atom gap is almost certainly smaller than the k-point and cutoff uncertainty, so I would not read it as physical stability ordering. Under the stated scope, that caveat does not change the verdict on what was computed. I see no admissible record that disagrees with the ordering. No follow-up tests are offered, and further DFT is not needed to decide this narrow claim, so I do not request it. No peers have spoken, so there are no peer claims to support or dispute. A useful falsification test for any broader ranking claim would be to converge k-mesh and cutoff for both cells and check whether the sign of the difference survives."}
